title: Ceiling on Event Services Agreements Held by One Client
content:
A client may hold a Private Event & Banquet Services agreement at more than one venue, because each venue carries its own diary, its own room rental and its own licence.

## The ceiling

1. No client holds more than two event services agreements at once, counting every agreement that is proposed, active or on hold.
2. Each agreement is written against exactly one venue, and every booking, deposit and bill belongs to the agreement its venue sits under.
3. Where a client wants events at a third venue, those events are booked into whichever of the two existing agreements covers that venue's operating company rather than opened as a third agreement.
4. A closed agreement does not count toward the ceiling, so a client who has closed an old venue agreement may open one at a new venue in its place.

## What the ceiling is counted from

The count of 2 is taken from the agreements the company's own records show standing for that client before a further agreement is opened, and not from the client's account of how many they hold. An agreement is matched to the client by the client organisation it is written for and to the venue by the venue it is written against; agreements standing against the same client are told apart by the day their term begins and the package they are written against. Only agreements in the proposed, active and on hold states are counted.

## Worked illustration on hypothetical records

A hypothetical client shows three agreements on the records: one active at a downtown venue, one on hold at a suburban venue, and one closed at a venue given up last year. Two of the three stand in a counted state, so the ceiling is reached and a further venue is served from one of those two. Were the suburban agreement also closed, only one agreement would stand in a counted state and a new venue agreement could be opened in its place.
